conviction_note: Implied event move 14.1% against a median 4.1% history, so abs_move set at 11; p_up 54 is a slight lean up. The reasons for it: a crowded short (19.9% of shares out, 6.8 days to cover, rising), the stock at its 52-week low and -48% since the CEO bought at $9.14 in September, and a >$50M FY guide that management reaffirmed on 2026-10-05, after Q3 had closed. Against that, Street FY $55.5M implies a Q4 of about $30M+, above the $17-18M recurring figure management described, and the August print, which reaffirmed the guide, was sold -3.2%. The findings net to +0.5 and the scaled number to +0.9. The two agree in sign and both are small next to the implied move, because the evidence is mostly public and balanced.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $12.8M and EPS about -$0.01 (Earnings Whispers preview 2026-11-10, https://finviz.com/news/420291/duos-technologies-must-prove-its-ai-data-center-pivot-is-producing-revenue-after-stock-halves). Chartmill also has $12.84M but EPS -$0.14, and Benzinga $12.6M (https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/DUOT/estimates, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DUOT/earnings-forecasts), so the revenue bar is sourced twice in agreement and the EPS bar is disputed. FY26: company guide >$50M revenue and positive adj. EBITDA, reaffirmed 2026-10-05 (https://finviz.com/news/398679/...); Street FY $55.5M. Q4 talking points from the Q2 call: recurring infrastructure revenue $17-18M and adj. EBITDA $8-10M. Preliminary 2027 framework >= $160M.
positioning_check: Short interest 6,250,901 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, up 451k from 10-15. That is 19.9% of 31.47M shares outstanding (float not reported, so % of float is higher), with 6.8 days to cover on 919k ADV; 09-30 was 6.10M and 11.5 days (https://equibles.com/stocks/duot/shortinterest). The baseline has no 25-delta skew (null). Put/call OI ratio is 0.83 and ATM IV 165%. The straddle implies a 16.2% move, 14.1% net of ordinary vol, against a median 4.1% / max 8.8% over the last 8 prints. Spot $4.78 is 1% above the 52-week low and -67% from the high; run-up -8.1% over 5 days and -12.8% over 20. Crowded short: this shrinks the negatives.

findings.finding: CFO reaffirmed FY2026 revenue >$50M and positive adjusted EBITDA on 2026-10-05, five days after Q3 closed (09-30) and with Q3 actuals in hand. With H1 revenue at $8.32M, that commits management to >= $41.7M in H2 (Q3 + Q4), against a Street Q3 of $12.8M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 print 2026-08-19: the >$50M guide was reaffirmed and the stock moved -3.16%. Q1 print (May): guide reaffirmed despite a revenue miss; baseline +8.82% on 2026-05-19. Reaffirmations have not reliably been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: The reaffirmation is public, but the stock has fallen from about $9 to $4.78 since. The market is discounting management's word, not missing it. If the post-quarter reaffirmation were priced, the stock would not be at its 52-week low with 20% of shares sold short. A print that shows Q3 largely delivered converts a doubted claim into a reported number.
findings.independence: The Q2 release (2026-08-17, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001396536/000107997326001150/ex99x1.htm) shows bookings of about $43.5M expected to be recognized in 2026, plus H1 $8.32M = about $51.8M, which supports the guide arithmetic. That is the same company, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: The Street's FY26 $55.5M with Q3 at $12.8M implies a Q4 of about $30-34M. That is well above the Q4 recurring infrastructure revenue of $17-18M management described on the Q2 call, and the company's own guide is only '>$50M'. The Street sits above what management has said, so the risk is that the year lands at $50-52M, beats the guide and misses consensus, or that Q4 language softens.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No FY guide cut has been recorded. The stock fell about 10% intraday after the Q1 miss despite the reaffirmation (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/duot-stock-q1-earnings-miss-report-ceo-says-50-million-doallar-target-still-within-reach-for-2026/cZXrVwnRemf).
findings.why_not_priced: The preview itself states that close to $30M in Q4 is required, so the arithmetic is public. What is not visible is whether the Street trims its $55.5M toward the guide. A stock already -67% from its high has partly priced a disappointment, which is why this is sized small.
findings.independence: The Q2 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/duos-technologies-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-17/) gives Q4 recurring of $17-18M. It is consistent with finding 1, not contradictory: FY >$50M can be met while the Street's $55.5M is missed.

findings.finding: On 09-30 Duos sold the GPUaaS SPV (2,304 B300 GPUs) to Axe Compute. Axe repaid about $87.8M of SPV debt and owes Duos $42.9M at $715k/month, due in full within 12 months or on any cluster financing. Duos now leases GPU capacity back from Axe to keep serving the Columbus customer under a revised 5-year contract. The Q2 10-Q said GPUaaS revenue would be booked gross as principal at margins >70%; buying capacity from Axe adds a lease cost, so the Q4 adj. EBITDA guide of $8-10M and the >70% margin claim are at risk of restatement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print on this line. The structure is new since the last print.
findings.why_not_priced: Neither the 8-K nor the release states the lease cost or the margin effect, and the Q3 print and call are the first time management must show Q4 economics after the sale. If the market had priced a margin cut, the Q4 EBITDA talking point would not still sit in the preview unchanged.
findings.independence: Axe's own 8-K and release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1446159/000117184326006386/exh_991.htm) say Duos covers colocation and energy costs for the cluster for 5 years, and that Axe expects $364.6M of customer revenue over the contract. The economics accrue to Axe, so this points the same way from a different filer.

findings.finding: Q3 GAAP will carry one-offs: a gain or loss on the 09-30 GPUaaS SPV sale; a gain or loss on the 08-05 rail (DTI) sale to Sandbank Acosta, a related party 50% owned by the then-interim CFO; and a tax benefit the 10-Q says 'substantially offsets' the 2026 tax liability. Headline EPS will be noisy against a disputed -$0.01 / -$0.14 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 had a $53.2M below-the-line gain (EPS $1.37 vs a $0.52 estimate on Benzinga) and the stock still moved -3.16%, so below-the-line items have not moved it.
findings.why_not_priced: The amounts are unquantified anywhere public. They are sized small because they sit below operating income with no path to the guide.
findings.independence: Shares a document (the 10-Q) with the financing finding; the SPV sale terms come from the 8-K used in the finding above.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-20 Duos announced a 10-year, 20 MW colocation contract, over $400M total contract value, with an unnamed publicly traded cloud services provider, deploying Q2 2027. It also announced about 100 MW of land being pursued (25 MW under contract), with all site agreements expected by year-end. This is the first contract signed since the Q2 print that supports the >= $160M 2027 framework, and the call is the first chance to frame 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Contract announcements were bought: the 55 MW Axe deal in August 'soared' (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/duot-stock-soars-five-year-agreements-worth-over-18x-2025-revenue/cZYG3fkRJ1K). But the stock is -12.8% over 20 days, which includes the Oct 20 announcement, so this one did not hold.
findings.why_not_priced: Public, and the price fell through it, so it is mostly priced. What is not priced is whether the call converts it into a firmed or raised 2027 number. The stock at $4.78 (market cap about $150M) against >$1B of claimed contract value says the market does not credit conversion.
findings.independence: The 8-K item 7.01 of 2026-10-20 is the same document (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001396536.json lists it). No other source.

findings.finding: Counterparty risk at Axe Compute (AGPU), which is the 55 MW / >$500M hosting customer, the obligor on the $42.9M deferred price, and now the GPU capacity lessor. Three directors, including Chairman Nuzum, resigned effective 2026-10-27, the CEO became Chair, and a new audit chair was named 11-09. Axe's Q3 results and call (call 2026-11-17 08:30 ET) fall inside the exit window and may update cluster go-live and the Duos sites.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a filing by a different company, with no wire coverage tying it to Duos. Customer concentration in Axe and Hydra Host is flagged generically in the preview, but the board turnover is not. If it were priced, the preview's risk list would mention it.
findings.independence: Axe's call notice (https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/AGPU/axe-compute-q3-2026-financial-results-call, 2026-11-11) sets the Nov 17 call. Axe's 11-13 8-K (new audit chair) shows the board being rebuilt, which slightly mitigates.

findings.finding: Crowded short into the print: 6.25M shares short (19.9% of shares outstanding, more of float) at the 10-30 settlement, up 451k, with 6.8 days to cover. The stock is 1% off its 52-week low. Any confirmation of Q3 delivery or Q4 run-rate has a squeeze mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +8.82% reaction on 2026-05-19 came while short interest was building (MarketBeat noted SI growth in April 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is itself the market's negative positioning. The asymmetry it creates, covering on any non-disappointment, is what is unpriced. An ATM IV of 165% shows the options market expects a big move, but there is no skew reading to say which way.
findings.independence: Earlier settlements (09-30: 6.10M, 11.5 days to cover) on the same page. Curved Trading had 4.5M in July (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/duot/short-interest/), showing the build.

findings.finding: Insiders bought on the open market in September: CEO Recker bought 9,250 shares at $9.14 on 09-22 (Form 4/A filed 10-15) and director Nixon 5,764 at $8.55 on 09-18. There have been no open-market sales in 12 months. Both buys are about 90% above today's $4.78.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and small in dollars ($134k total). It is signal, not flow, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The EDGAR submissions list shows the Form 4 on 09-22 and the 4/A on 10-15 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001396536.json).

findings.finding: Reporting and control risk. The Q2 10-Q was late (NT 10-Q on 08-17: the auditor needed more time). The CFO is new (DeAlmeida, effective 08-24) after an interim CFO who owned 50% of the related-party buyer of the rail unit. This is the first quarter-close under the new CFO and includes two divestitures. A repeat late 10-Q or restated figures would hit a stock already distrusted.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the August NT 10-Q the print still came on 08-19 and moved -3.16%.
findings.why_not_priced: The preview names the 'ongoing CFO transition' as a risk, so it is partly priced. The specific auditor-delay history and related-party sale are buried in filings.
findings.independence: The 8-K of 2026-10-09 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1396536/000107997326001340/duot_8k.htm) gives the CFO and CLO agreements. The 10-Q subsequent-events note gives the related-party rail sale.

findings.finding: Capital needs. About 100 MW of land and the Axe JV (up to $140M equity commitment) need funding. The June raise included $36.1M of pre-funded warrants not in the 31.47M outstanding count. Cash was $112.3M at 06-30 before the $15M Columbus purchase. A raise or ATM at or after the call is possible, and this stock fell after past financings. But the money would fund contracted demand ($400M CSP contract, $500M Axe hosting, $111M hyperscaler), so it is signed near zero.
findings.why_not_priced: No financing is announced. A raise at a $150M market cap would be heavily dilutive, which may explain part of the drawdown, so it is probably partly priced.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers preview flags GPU senior-debt timing and the Axe JV financing as risks (https://finviz.com/news/420291/...). The 10-Q is shared with the one-off finding.

outside_window.finding: Axe 55 MW hosting: readiness targeted late 2026 into early 2027, and billing needs Axe's written acceptance. Revenue conversion resolves in coming quarters, not at this print.
The 20 MW CSP contract deploys in Q2 2027, so its revenue sits outside any window here.
FINRA short interest for the 11-13 settlement publishes about 11-24, after the window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew reading. The run-up (-12.8% over 20 days, -67% from the high, at the 52-week low) and a rising 20% short interest say the market is positioned for disappointment. My balanced-to-slightly-positive read cuts against that positioning but not against an option signal, and it leans on the squeeze mechanism rather than on an unpriced company number. That is why p_up is only 54.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction): the August print reaffirmed the guide and moved -3.16%, so the post-quarter reaffirmation finding went from +1.5 to +1.0.

Lesson 7 (a crowded short shrinks negatives): with 19.9% of shares out short and 6.8 days to cover, the Street-above-mgmt Q4 finding went from -1.5 to -1.2 and the GPU lease-margin finding from -0.8 to -0.6.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the money would fund contracted capacity ($400M, $500M, $111M contracts), so the capital-needs finding went from -0.5 to -0.2.
Lesson 2 (one-offs): the divestiture gain/loss and tax item went from -0.3 to -0.2, below operating income with no path to the guide.
Lesson 6: the revenue bar is sourced twice in agreement ($12.8M / $12.84M); the EPS bar is disputed (-$0.01 vs -$0.14), so no finding is sized on EPS. Post-window items moved to outside_window.
With the net lean slightly more positive, p_up moved from 53 to 54.
